function: Over-the-air aggregation of LoRA adapter gradients in federated LLM fine-tuning: MIMO-OFDM AirComp transceiver with hybrid beamforming, rank selection and sub-carrier allocation (p. 2-3, 5).
system: BS: Nr=32 antennas, Nf=8 RF chains; K=8 devices with Nu=4 antennas; N=16 OFDM sub-carriers (512 in fine-tuning runs); no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 10, 12).
method: Federated LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs (GPT2-Small, OpenLLaMA-3B, Llama-7B) over AirComp; beamforming by alternating and manifold optimization, rank and sub-carrier selection by heuristic backtracking, not learned (p. 3, 8-10).
data_channel: Simulated geometry-based Saleh-Valenzuela MIMO-OFDM channel with large-scale fading, devices random within 100 m (p. 5, 10); text datasets HealthCareMagic and OpenOrca for LLM fine-tuning (p. 10).
test_conditions: Four runs (three LLMs, two datasets), each evaluated by perplexity on the validation dataset; beamformer MSE swept over K, M, Nr, N; no unseen scenario (p. 10-13).
baselines: AirComp: FD-AO, HB-CD [34], HB-MO, HB-RD, HB-ZF; fine-tuning: AirFL-NS, Ideal-FL, AirFL-QuLoRA [51], AirFL-Prompt-Tuning [52], AirFL-P-Tuning [53] (p. 10-11).
metrics: Computation MSE of AirComp, training loss, perplexity on the validation dataset, average number of transmitted gradient symbols (p. 10-13).
complexity: Worst-case order: Algorithm 1 O(I(MNK(Nu+Nf+2Iiter Nf^2 Nr^2)+KNr)); Algorithm 2 O(R(2+O1)); no runtime measured (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 5: "Saleh-Valenzuela model" is a custom geometry-based simulated channel (Eq. 8); no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned anywhere.
q2_support: p. 13: "the average PPL on the validation dataset"; p. 10: "K = 8 WDs deployed randomly within a radius of 100 m". Each LLM is fine-tuned and evaluated in one setting; the sweeps of K, M, Nr, N (p. 11) are for the optimized beamformer, so no trained model is tested on an unseen condition.
q3_support: p. 10: "coordinate descent-based method given in [34]" (HB-CD) and "HB-RD: Hybrid beamforming, where Ut is set randomly", compared on computation MSE (p. 10-11); p. 11: "AirFL-Prompt-Tuning: Prompt-Tuning [52] is utilized" and "are quantified as in [51]" (QuLoRA), compared on loss and perplexity; p. 12: "outperforms all baselines (except Ideal-FL)".
q4_support: p. 9: "The worst-case complexity of Algorithm 1" is O(I(MNK(Nu+Nf+2Iiteration Nf^2 Nr^2)+KNr)) and that of Algorithm 2 is O(R(2+O1)): the cost of the AirComp transceiver and the rank and sub-carrier design.
q5_support: p. 10: "HealthCareMagic and OpenOrca" are text datasets of the learning task alone; the channel is simulated (p. 5) and the paper gives no code or data link (the only URLs are references and the article DOI, p. 1).
notes: Included as area 7: the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation of LoRA gradients (MIMO-OFDM AirComp, hybrid beamforming, rank selection, sub-carrier allocation) and the learned element is the LLM adapter trained across devices; beamforming and selection are optimization-based, not learned (Eqs. 31-36, Algorithms 1-2). q3 rests on HB-CD [34] and the random-Ut HB-RD for MSE and on QuLoRA [51], Prompt-Tuning [52], P-Tuning [53] for loss and perplexity; reviewer to confirm that these count as earlier published aggregation or learned baselines.
